questions.text: Teacher Digital Literacy: Assess ability to use EdTech: (1) Basic computer/smartphone skills; (2) Ability to use LMS/SIS; (3) Troubleshooting basic issues; (4) Online pedagogy (teaching via Zoom/WhatsApp); (5) Digital content creation; (6) Cyber safety awareness; (7) Training frequency.
questions.evidence_required: Digital literacy assessment results, Training logs, Usage analytics
questions.africa_specific_notes: Teachers often less tech-savvy than students. Hardware deployed often sits unused because teachers can't use it.

questions.text: Pedagogical Competence: Assess teaching quality: (1) Subject matter mastery; (2) Learner-centered methods (vs rote learning); (3) Classroom management (large classes); (4) Inclusive teaching (special needs); (5) Assessment skills (formative vs summative); (6) Continuous Professional Development (CPD); (7) Certification status.
questions.evidence_required: Lesson observation reports, CPD records, Student performance data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Rote learning dominant. Shift to CBC (Competency Based Curriculum) requires massive re-training. Large class sizes (50-100) challenge pedagogy.

questions.text: Foundational Literacy & Numeracy: Assess core skills: (1) Reading fluency (grade level); (2) Basic numeracy; (3) Language of instruction mastery (English/French vs Mother Tongue); (4) Remedial support availability; (5) Assessment frequency; (6) Learning poverty rate; (7) Transition readiness.
questions.evidence_required: Standardized test scores (EGRA/EGMA), Report cards, Remedial program data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Learning poverty high (10-year-olds can't read). EdTech must address foundations before advanced topics. Language barrier is huge.

questions.text: Digital & 21st Century Skills: Assess future readiness: (1) Digital literacy (using devices/internet); (2) Coding/Computational thinking; (3) Critical thinking & problem solving; (4) Collaboration skills; (5) Financial literacy; (6) Online safety awareness; (7) Employability skills.
questions.evidence_required: Digital skills assessment, Project portfolios, Employer feedback
questions.africa_specific_notes: Digital divide means many leave school without touching a computer. Mobile-first digital skills essential.

questions.text: School Leadership & Management: Assess admin capacity: (1) Financial management (budgeting, fee collection); (2) Strategic planning; (3) Staff management (hiring, retention); (4) Infrastructure maintenance planning; (5) Community engagement; (6) Data management (EMIS usage); (7) Crisis management.
questions.evidence_required: School development plan, Financial audits, Staff retention data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Head teachers often promoted for seniority, not management skills. Financial mismanagement common.

questions.text: EdTech Implementation Capacity: Ability to deploy technology: (1) IT support staff availability; (2) Change management strategy; (3) Device management policy; (4) Helpdesk responsiveness; (5) Vendor relationship management; (6) Pilot evaluation skills; (7) Sustainability planning.
questions.evidence_required: IT support logs, Implementation plan, Device inventory
questions.africa_specific_notes: Schools often receive donated tech but lack capacity to maintain it. 'Graveyards' of computers common.

questions.text: UX for Low Literacy/Digital Skills: Design for context: (1) Intuitive navigation (icons vs text); (2) Voice/Audio instructions; (3) Local language interfaces; (4) Minimal steps to access content; (5) Error tolerance (easy to undo); (6) Onboarding simplicity; (7) Accessibility features.
questions.evidence_required: UX testing reports, User feedback, Interface screenshots
questions.africa_specific_notes: Apps designed for West often fail. Users may be first-time smartphone users. Text-heavy UIs fail.

questions.text: Gamification & Engagement: Keeping students motivated: (1) Age-appropriate gamification (points, badges); (2) Streak mechanics (daily usage); (3) Social learning features (leaderboards?); (4) Feedback loops (immediate correction); (5) Notification strategy (nudges); (6) Content interactivity; (7) Retention rates.
questions.evidence_required: Engagement metrics (DAU/MAU), Retention curves, Gamification design doc
questions.africa_specific_notes: Self-paced learning requires high motivation. Gamification helps, but must not distract from learning.

scoring_notes: Layer 4 (Competence) for Education in SSA: Teacher digital literacy is the bottleneck for EdTech. Student foundational literacy is the crisis. UX must accommodate low digital exposure.
